sampling_model.design: Two-fold cross-fitting under i.i.d. sampling from \(P\in\mathcal P_4\).
sampling_model.overlap: Censoring follow-up satisfies \(G_a(t\mid x)=(1-t)^2g_a(t,x)\) and vanishes at the fixed horizon.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Treatment propensity, event hazard, and rescaled censoring residual are unknown and learned foldwise by the endpoint local-cubic handle; no estimator-side rate is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4 gives a cross-fitted asymptotic-linear survival estimator under a uniform censoring floor and high-level nuisance product rates, and Section 5.3 obtains RMST inference by integration.
Theorem A1 gives a Gaussian limit for an unadjusted Kaplan--Meier RMST integral at the support endpoint under a finite weighted tail integral.
The paper develops efficient covariate-adjusted RMST estimation for randomized trials at an ordinary fixed follow-up horizon.
Theorem 1 gives whole-support local-polynomial conditional-density rates under nondegenerate local information and a smooth positive design density.
Theorem 3.2 gives pointwise asymptotic normality for local-polynomial Nelson--Aalen hazard smoothing strictly below the upper support boundary.
Self-normalized Gaussian approximation for independent sums is available under finite \(2+\delta\) moments.

The paper gives cross-fitted debiased inference for smooth counterfactual survival functionals, including survival integrals, under left-truncated right-censored sampling and high-level nuisance conditions; it does not derive primitive exact-quadratic terminal-cell rates, weak-moment Studentization, or efficiency at a vanishing-censoring endpoint.

body.tldr: In a designed-depletion or calibrated loss-to-follow-up regime, the censoring time is the earlier of two conditionally independent continuous loss or availability times whose near-horizon survivals vanish linearly, giving the known quadratic endpoint order while leaving the smooth residual censoring law unknown. At the scientific horizon, this quadratic censoring makes the influence function for survival itself non-square-integrable, but the remaining-life factor in fixed-endpoint RMST cancels one endpoint power and leaves a finite efficiency bound. The paper constructs a total cross-fitted one-step estimator with a uniform expansion over the stated radius-20 H\"older primitive class while learning the treatment propensity, event hazard, and rescaled censoring residual. At every interior law, normalized smooth censoring-density tilts preserve the exact quadratic factor, all finite smooth generating submodels are differentiable in quadratic mean and hence locally asymptotically normal, and compactness plus observed-law identifiability extend estimator regularity to every relevant in-class DQM local alternative. Simultaneous local-cubic concentration in the last time--covariate cells gives nuisance rate \( (\log n/n)^{1/3} \), and a terminal-strip Fano packing proves a matching minimax sup-norm lower bound for learning the event hazard over the same primitive class. This sharp primitive rate, exact product drift, weak \(5/2\)-moment Studentization, full endpoint-efficiency certificate, and uniform Wald coverage form the publishable kernel.

project_justification.gap: Westling et al. establish machine-learning inference for treatment-specific survival and integrated RMST under a censoring floor and high-level nuisance-rate conditions. Morenz, Wolock, and Carone develop debiased machine learning for smooth counterfactual survival functionals under left truncation and right censoring, again using high-level nuisance conditions rather than deriving a primitive exact-quadratic endpoint rate. Classical endpoint Kaplan--Meier theory permits vanishing follow-up for integrated functionals but has no conditional confounding adjustment or learned nuisance blocks. Existing local-polynomial hazard theory does not supply uniform last-cell concentration when the predictable risk set collapses quadratically, and generic convolution theory does not itself verify censoring paths, LAN, or full-model estimator regularity for this endpoint experiment.
project_justification.niche: The nonempty niche is a fixed-target efficiency theorem on a primitive smooth class where survival-at-endpoint inference is irregular, RMST remains regular, the nuisance fits must preserve the known quadratic factor, and the feasible score may lack a third moment.
project_justification.fill: The project integrates the survival score before analysis, learns the smooth event hazard and \(q_a=S_ag_a\) by explicit boundary-adaptive cubic risk-set equations, proves their terminal-cell \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\) rate without assuming it, and matches the event-hazard upper rate by a same-class terminal-strip Fano lower bound. It propagates the exact product drift through cross-fitting and proves variance consistency and a uniform Studentized limit from a \(5/2\)-moment envelope. At interior laws it constructs normalized censoring-density tilts that retain \(G_a(t\mid x)=(1-t)^2g_a(t,x)\), verifies DQM and i.i.d. LAN for all finite smooth generators, proves tangent density, and uses compactness, identifiability, endpoint score continuity, and the uniform expansion to establish regularity along every relevant in-class DQM local alternative before applying the convolution bound.

body.related_work: Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024) is the closest treatment-specific survival reference: its Theorem 4 supplies a cross-fitted asymptotic-linear survival estimator under a censoring floor and high-level nuisance product rates, and Section 5.3 obtains RMST inference by integrating the survival-process limit. Morenz, Wolock, and Carone (2024), arXiv:2411.09017, is the closest broader survival-functional DML comparator: it treats smooth counterfactual survival functionals, including survival integrals, with flexible nuisance learning under left-truncated right-censored sampling, but it does not derive the exact-quadratic primitive nuisance rate, the weak-moment Studentization argument, or efficiency at a horizon where censoring survival vanishes. Tian et al. (2020), Theorem A1, and Stute (1995) show that an unadjusted Kaplan--Meier integral can retain a Gaussian endpoint limit under a weighted tail condition; they neither adjust for conditional confounding nor learn the present conditional nuisance blocks. Diaz et al. (2019) establish efficient covariate-adjusted RMST estimation in randomized trials with ordinary follow-up. Cattaneo et al. (2024), Theorem 1 and Appendix A.5, provide normalized local-polynomial bases and boundary-uniform Gram arguments under nondegenerate information and a smooth positive design density; here the terminal risk degenerates and \(f\) may be only measurable within its band. Jiang and Doksum (2003), equations (2.5)--(2.8) and Theorems 3.2 and 3.4, provide local-polynomial Nelson--Aalen algebra but restrict asymptotics below an upper boundary with positive risk. Fan and Guerre (2016) provide whole-support polynomial reproduction and boundary geometry, while their smooth-design condition is replaced here by a density-band sandwich. Munch et al. (2024), Theorem 9 and Corollary 13, give integrated conditional-hazard rates under positive endpoint follow-up; Efromovich (2024) gives mean-integrated-squared-error theory rather than simultaneous terminal sup-norm control. Stone (1982) supplies the classical H\"older minimax benchmark but not censoring-depleted terminal information. Jing, Shao, and Wang (2003) supply a weak-moment self-normalization template, and Chernozhukov et al. (2018) supply cross-fit conditioning and orthogonal product-remainder organization. Van der Vaart (1998), Theorems 7.2 and 25.20, supplies the generic DQM-to-LAN and scalar convolution machinery; the present proof constructs the event and censoring submodels, establishes their DQM property and tangent density, and proves regularity for arbitrary relevant in-class DQM local alternatives before invoking that machinery.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The decisive terminal-cell kill test is discharged by thm:primitive-endpoint-concentration. Its proof establishes an at-risk Gram of order \(Mh_M^4\), preserves coercivity under an arbitrary measurable density \(f\), controls the martingale numerator and Taylor remainder simultaneously, and makes low-count fallbacks uniformly negligible. Formalization must preserve those coupled bounds; weakening them to an \(n^{-1/4}\) nuisance rate would no longer imply the headline expansion. Numerical values from the presolve witness are diagnostics and are not theorem claims.
body.honest_scope: Identification of the fixed contrast is standard. Estimation, variance consistency, and inference at the quadratic endpoint are uniform over the stated primitive class, whereas convolution efficiency is pointwise at each interior law. The efficiency proof includes normalized compact-time censoring-density tilts, proves by integration by parts that their residual survivals retain the exact quadratic factor and \(C^{3,1}\) regularity, verifies DQM and LAN for the finite smooth generators, and establishes estimator regularity along every relevant DQM local alternative that remains in \(\mathcal P_4\). No efficiency claim is made at boundary laws. The theorem fixes horizon \(1\), censoring exponent \(2\), one-dimensional covariate, smoothness order \(4\), and all radius and band constants. Within this class, the learned event-hazard sup-norm rate \((\log n/n)^{1/3}\) is minimax sharp; the converse is not a minimax lower bound for RMST risk or for each other nuisance. The result does not cover an estimated endpoint exponent, a shorter moving horizon, a parametric hazard subclass, or a different target. For an in-class sanity check, fixing \(\delta\in(0,1)\), setting \(\tau=1-\delta\), and diagnostically restricting the same factor-preserving learner and score to \([0,\tau]\) gives \(G_a(t\mid x)\ge\delta^2/2\), the ordinary positive-follow-up regime covered by Westling et al. (2024). This diagnostic restriction does not alter the main horizon \(1\) target. The general censoring-exponent phase diagram remains separate.
